---
title: "Ex1 - Getting and knowing your Data (World Food Facts) - Solutions"
output: html_document
---

### Step 1. Go to https://www.kaggle.com/openfoodfacts/world-food-facts/data

### Step 2. Download the dataset to your computer and unzip it.

```{r step1, message=FALSE}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
```

### Step 3. Use the tsv file and assign it to a dataframe called food

```{r}
# change the path to the place where you unzipped the file
food <- read_tsv("~/Desktop/en.openfoodfacts.org.products.tsv",
                 guess_max = 100000) # look at more rows to guess the column types
```

### Step 4. See the first 5 entries

```{r}
head(food, 5)
```

### Step 5. What is the number of observations in the dataset?

```{r}
dim(food)  # will give you both (observations/rows, columns)
nrow(food) # will give you only the observations/rows number
```

### Step 6. What is the number of columns in the dataset?

```{r}
dim(food)  # will give you both (observations/rows, columns)
ncol(food) # will give you only the columns number

# OR

glimpse(food) # Columns: 163
```

### Step 7. Print the name of all the columns.

```{r}
names(food)
```

### Step 8. What is the name of 105th column?

```{r}
# R counts from 1, so the 105th column is simply column 105
names(food)[105]
```

### Step 9. What is the type of the observations of the 105th column?

```{r}
class(food[[105]])
```

### Step 10. How is the dataset indexed?

```{r}
# tibbles have no index: rows are identified by their position, 1 to n
range(seq_len(nrow(food)))
```

### Step 11. What is the product name of the 19th observation?

```{r}
food$product_name[19]

# or by position (product_name is the 8th column)
food[[19, 8]]
```
